'''Françoise Cyrot-Lackmann''', (born 1940), is a French [[Condensed matter physics|condensed-matter]] [[physicist]], and research director at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]]. She co-founded the association [[Femmes et Sciences]] (Women and Science) and led the French government's Mission for Parity in Science and Technology. She is known for her promotion of [[gender parity]] in science and technology as well as for her work as a physicist.

== Early life and education ==
Françoise Lackmann was born in 1940<ref>{{Cite web |title=Francoise Lackmann : SCI FRANMI |url=https://www.pappers.fr/dirigeant/francoise_lackmann_1940-06 |access-date=2026-08-07 |website=Pappers |language=fr}}</ref> in [[La Baule-Escoublac|La Baule]] ([[Loire-Atlantique]]). She gained a doctorate in physics 1968 at the [[Laboratoire de Physique des Solides|Laboratory of Solid-State Physics]] in [[Ormoy, Essonne|Orsay (Essonne).]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2002-01-27 |title=Françoise Cyrot-Lackmann, un combat au nom des femmes de  science |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/2002/01/27/francoise-cyrot-lackmann-un-combat-au-nom-des-femmes-de-science_4206091_1819218.html |access-date=2026-08-07 |work=Le Monde |language=fr |issn=1950-6244}}</ref>

== Career ==
Cyrot-Lackmann was appointed [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS) scientific delegate for the [[Rhône-Alpes]] region in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Françoise Cyrot-Lackmann |url=https://jorfsearch.steinertriples.ch/name/Fran%C3%A7oise%20Cyrot-Lackmann |access-date=2026-08-07 |website=JORFSearch}}</ref>

From 1989 to 1996, she directed the Laboratory for the Study of Electronic Properties of Solids in [[Grenoble]].<ref name=":0" />

In 2000, Cyrot-Lackmann founded the Association [[Femmes et Sciences]] (Women in Science) with fellow scientists [[Huguette Delavault]], [[Françoise Gaspard]], [[Claudine Hermann]], [[Colette Kreder]] and [[Femmes et Mathématiques|l’association femmes et mathématiques]].<ref name=":1" /> In November 2000, she provided figures for the percentage of women biologists in France (45%) and for physics and maths (15%).<ref name=":2" />

In 2001, she was appointed head of the French government office, Mission for Parity in Science and Technology (MPST). The MPST created the [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize]] in the same year. In 2002, MPST was due to receive over 300,00 Euros to promote the participation of women in France in science.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Mertl |first=Melissa |date=14 December 2001 |title=France Addresses Gender Gap in Science |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/france-addresses-gender-gap-science |access-date=8 August 2026}}</ref>

Cyrot-Lackmann has written about the gender gap in science.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kumar (Ed.) |first=Neelam |title=Gender and Science: Studies across Cultures |publisher=[[Foundation Books]] |year=2012 |isbn=978-93-82264-96-5 |pages=227–263}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hermann |first=Claudine |last2=Cyrot-Lackmann |first2=Françoise |date=December 2002 |title=Women in Science in France |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/science-in-context/article/women-in-science-in-france/85768257865490E66C8A4D382579ABE3 |journal=[[Science in Context (journal)]] |language=en |volume=15 |issue=4 |pages=529–556 |doi=10.1017/S0269889702000637 |issn=1474-0664}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Citation |last=Hermann |first=Claudine |chapter=Women in Science in France |date=2012 |title=Gender and Science: Studies across Cultures |pages=227–263 |editor-last=Kumar |editor-first=Neelam |chapter-url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/gender-and-science/women-in-science-in-france/1C3445775364C96B41262AD8FB3362C1 |access-date=2026-08-07 |publisher=Foundation Books |isbn=978-81-7596-925-4 |last2=Cyrot-Lackmann |first2=Françoise |last3=Peifer |first3=Jeanne |last4=Rouch |first4=Hélène}}</ref> In 2026, as part of the Association Femmes & Sciences she pushed for [[List of women's names for the Eiffel Tower|72 women scientists]] to be commemorated in the [[List of names on the Eiffel Tower|list of names on the Eiffel tower]].<ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 Femmes de Science pour la Tour Eiffel] pdf [[Femmes et Sciences]] (in French) Accessed 8 August 2026</ref>

Cyrot-Lackmann's key contribution to condensed-matter physics is the development of the moment method for calculating the local electronic density of states (DOS) of solids within the tight-binding approximation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cyrot-Lackmann |first=Françoise |date=July 1969 |title=On the calculation of surface tension in transition metals |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/003960286990140X?via%3Dihub |journal=[[Surface Science]] |volume=15 |issue=3 |pages=535–548}}</ref>
